knowledge.statement: A leader that receives MsgReadIndex postpones the request (appends it to r.pendingReadIndexMessages and returns without answering) exactly when its current configuration is not a singleton and r.committedEntryInCurrentTerm() is false, i.e. when the entry at its committed index was issued by an earlier term.
knowledge.conditions: Local raft instance in StateLeader; message type MsgReadIndex; configuration not a singleton (tracker.IsSingleton() false).

knowledge.statement: Postponed ReadIndex requests are released only from the MsgAppResp success path when r.maybeCommit() reports that the commit index advanced to an entry of the leader's term; the helper refuses to release them when committedEntryInCurrentTerm() is false.
knowledge.conditions: StateLeader; MsgAppResp handling for which pr.MaybeUpdate or the probe-recovery condition is true; releasePendingReadIndexMessages is the only consumer of pendingReadIndexMessages.

knowledge.statement: switchToConfig is a second code path on which a leader can perform the term's first commit: when the configuration returned by the conforming changer raises ProgressTracker.Committed() above raftLog.committed and the entry at that index carries the leader's current term, it calls r.maybeCommit() and, on success, only broadcasts appends; it does not release pendingReadIndexMessages.
knowledge.conditions: StateLeader with a non-empty voter set; called from applyConfChange (application applies a committed configuration change) with the leader's Progress values already reflecting quorum-level acknowledgement of a current-term entry.

knowledge.statement: A postponed request is not part of readOnly.unconfirmedReads, so readOnly.heartbeatCtx() returns nil, outgoing heartbeats carry no read context, and the MsgHeartbeatResp handler returns early on an empty context: a periodic heartbeat round cannot release a postponed request.
knowledge.conditions: ReadOnlySafe; pendingReadIndexMessages non-empty while readOnly.unconfirmedReads is empty.

knowledge.statement: The library permits an application to report applied progress (Advance / MsgStorageApplyResp) while it is still applying the entries of a previous Ready, and it fixes no ordering between that progress report and the required ApplyConfChange call for a committed configuration change; the campaign gate hasUnappliedConfChanges() reads raftLog.applied only.
knowledge.conditions: Node/RawNode consumer following the documented Ready/Advance contract.

knowledge.statement: ProgressTracker.IsSingleton returns true exactly when Voters[0] has one member and Voters[1] is empty; it never compares the single voter with the local node id, although its doc comment says the single voting member is the leader.
knowledge.conditions: tracker.ProgressTracker of any raft instance, including one that is no longer a member of its configuration.

knowledge.statement: stepLeader answers MsgReadIndex immediately - with a local ReadState for a local request, or with MsgReadIndexResp for a forwarded one - whenever tracker.IsSingleton() is true, using r.raftLog.committed and without sending any heartbeat or consulting readOnly; otherwise it requires committedEntryInCurrentTerm() and a readOnly round.

When the configuration change that removes the local node is applied while the node is leading, switchToConfig keeps it leading unless Config.StepDownOnRemoval (false by default) is set; the MsgProp path explicitly refuses proposals from a leader that is not in the configuration ('If we are not currently a member of the range ... drop any new proposals') while the MsgReadIndex path has no equivalent guard.
knowledge.conditions: StateLeader; applyConfChange on a committed change whose resulting configuration does not contain the local node; Config.StepDownOnRemoval false (the default).

knowledge.statement: node.run sets its proposal channel to nil when an applied configuration change removes the local node from Progress and that node appears in neither cs.Voters nor cs.VotersOutgoing, and restores the channel from n.propc only in the branch that reacts to a change of r.lead with a leader known; applying a change that adds the node back does not restore the channel.
knowledge.conditions: Node wrapper (node.run) driven through ApplyConfChange; the removal is applied while the node is in Progress and the addition is applied while it is not.

knowledge.statement: With the proposal channel nil - either because the node was removed or because no leader is known - Node.Propose sends into a nil channel inside a select that also watches the caller's context and the node's done channel, so the call blocks until one of those fires and then returns ctx.Err() or ErrStopped.
knowledge.conditions: Node.Propose/stepWait with the run loop's propc variable nil.

knowledge.statement: ReadOnlyLeaseBased cannot be combined with CheckQuorum disabled (Config.validate rejects it), and with CheckQuorum enabled a voter inside its election-timeout lease ignores a vote request from a higher term, so while the remaining voters still hear a leader they will not elect another one; a removed leader that keeps being answered therefore keeps a live lease rather than serving stale lease-based reads, and when the voters stop answering, its own quorum check fails and it steps down.
knowledge.conditions: Cluster whose remaining voters still answer the removed leader's heartbeats; ReadOnlyLeaseBased with CheckQuorum enabled (the only accepted combination).

knowledge.statement: The Node wrapper closes its proposal channel only when an applied configuration change makes the local node's Progress entry disappear (the guard requires the node to have been in Progress before, to be absent after, and to appear in neither Voters nor VotersOutgoing); a demotion to learner keeps the Progress entry and therefore does not close the channel, and applying a change that adds the node back takes the okBefore=false path, so an addition never re-opens a channel that a removal closed. The only site that re-opens it is the branch that reacts to a change of r.lead while a leader is known.
knowledge.conditions: Node wrapper driven through ApplyConfChange; Config.StepDownOnRemoval false so the node can keep leading or following without its Progress entry being removed.

knowledge.statement: Node.Propose cannot report a closed proposal channel as such: with the channel nil the call waits on a select over that channel, the caller's context and the node's done channel, so it returns only ctx.Err() or ErrStopped, which are the same results an ordinary lost proposal or a stopped node produces.
knowledge.conditions: Node.Propose/stepWait while node.run has set propc to nil.

knowledge.statement: The end of a removed leader's ReadIndex exposure does not follow from the quorum option alone: it follows from a replacement leader being elected. In the single-voter remainder the remaining voter elects itself, and under PreVote the remaining voters grant a new election, so the removed leader learns of the higher term after one heartbeat tick; with CheckQuorum and a remainder of more than one voter the voters keep answering the removed leader's heartbeats, refuse each other's vote requests while inside their election-timeout lease, and elect nobody, so the removed leader keeps leading, keeps its lease, and finishes subsequent read-only rounds from its own frozen commit index - and it begins that election on the leader's own acknowledgement of the round (sendMsgReadIndexResponse adds the local ack before broadcasting heartbeats), an ack that belongs to a node which is not a voter of the configuration whose quorum the round needed.
knowledge.conditions: Cluster with CheckQuorum enabled; a leading node that the application removed from the configuration while Config.StepDownOnRemoval is false; the resulting configuration has more than one voter; those voters still hear and answer the removed leader's heartbeats and their own election timers do not expire; ReadOnlySafe.

knowledge.statement: A follower that receives MsgReadIndex forwards it to the leader it knows (raising no term, since MsgReadIndex is treated as a local message). If that leader has been removed from a configuration whose single voter is another node and is still leading, the request takes the singleton shortcut and the leader answers it with a MsgReadIndexResp carrying its own frozen commit index; the forwarding node consumes that answer as its own ReadState and, once it advances past that index, serves reads that can miss entries the actual leader of the reduced configuration had already committed.
knowledge.conditions: ReadOnlySafe; a requester node whose r.lead is a node that is leading but is not a voter of its own configuration, with exactly one voter in that configuration; the requester's request is delivered to that leader before the requester hears from the new term.

knowledge.statement: If a ReadIndex request reaches a still-leading but removed node whose configuration has more than one voter, the singleton shortcut does not apply, so the request is taken into readOnly (the leader adds it and broadcasts heartbeats) and is answered only if the round completes. When the leadership then ends - the removed leader learns of the higher term from a voter that answers a lower-term message, or its own read-only round cannot reach the configuration's quorum - whatever it accepted is gone: no ReadState, nothing left pending or unconfirmed, and no refusal signalled to the caller, so an application that treats acceptance as a promise waits out its own deadline, and only one that retries unconditionally recovers.
knowledge.conditions: ReadOnlySafe; a leading node that the application removed from the configuration while Config.StepDownOnRemoval is false; the reduced configuration has more than one voter; the request is delivered while the removed leader's committed entry is from its own term (so the postpone path is not taken).

scope.description: Observe the whole interval of one postponed ReadIndex request on a real 4-node group: the leader postpones it, the application then applies an already-committed configuration change whose resulting configuration commits the leader's first entry of the term, the acknowledgement of the previous configuration arrives late, a heartbeat round runs, and finally an unrelated proposal is committed.
assumptions: Four voters {1,2,3,4} bootstrapped from a ConfState-only snapshot, with log entries 1..9 ordinary and entry 10 the configuration change, HardState{Term:1, Commit:10}, applied index 10 (the application has reported applied progress but has not yet called ApplyConfChange for entry 10, which node.go:166-187 permits).

Transport preserves raft's per-message semantics (each message is Stepped by its target and resulting messages are delivered in order); voters are reachable for votes; voter 4 is unreachable and voter 3's append acknowledgements are delayed, which is the message-loss/delay part of the fault model.
The applied change is taken from the log entry at index 10 exactly as an application does when it applies CommittedEntries.
excluded: Pre-vote, check-quorum and lease-based reads (all disabled by the test configuration stub).
Snapshot-based recovery and asynchronous storage writes.

basis.prefix: For each case: build four nodes whose storage is bootstrapped with the case ConfState (voters {1,2,3,4}, or the joint configuration voters {1,2,3} + voters_outgoing {1,2,3,4}), append ten term-1 entries with entry 10 the case configuration change, persist HardState{Term:1,Commit:10} and set Applied=10; then elect node 1 with a real MsgHup/MsgVote/MsgVoteResp round (voter 4 unreachable, voter 3's MsgAppResp delayed), deliver the client's MsgReadIndex, apply the committed change at index 10 via applyConfChange, deliver the delayed acknowledgement, run one heartbeat round (tick), and finally propose one unrelated entry.
basis.requirement: A ReadIndex request that a leader accepts by postponing (raft.go:1363-1368) must be answered once the leader has committed an entry of its term, whichever path performs that commit (raft.go:1550-1554 for the MsgAppResp path, raft.go:2013-2028 for the switchToConfig path), because the helper that discharges the duty is guarded only by committedEntryInCurrentTerm() (raft.go:2127-2145) and the caller's comment states the release is due once the committed index has progressed for the term.
basis.responsibility: raft (target): the leader is the producer of the answer for a request it accepted, and switchToConfig is part of raft, not of the application.

comparisons.description: Precondition observation: the leader postponed the received request because no entry of its term was committed (committed_entry_term 1, leader_term 2).

Witness: applying the committed removal of voter 4 performed the leader's first commit of term 2 (committed 10 -> 11, committed_entry_term 2 == leader_term), so the postponed request is due to be answered, but it is still pending and no ReadState was produced.
Variant of the same cause: applying the committed zero change left the joint configuration, so the incoming half committed the leader's first term-2 entry, yet the postponed request is still pending.

No repair from the periodic round: two heartbeats are sent with an empty read context (heartbeat_ctx_len 0), the delayed acknowledgement of the previous configuration is already in place (match_3 11), and no ReadState is produced.

Control: an unrelated proposal committed by the new configuration releases the postponed request (released_request_ctx A), so the release mechanism works and is reached only through the MsgAppResp commit path.
Control for the joint variant: the postponed request is only released once the unrelated proposal is committed.

scope.description: Observe what raft answers for a ReadIndex request that arrives at a node which the application removed from its configuration while it was leading (StepDownOnRemoval false), after the remaining voter has become leader of the reduced single-voter configuration and committed an entry the removed leader never receives.

comparisons.description: The node whose removal the application applied is still leading, with a configuration whose single voter is another node (singleton true, is_voter false).

Control: the same request answered by the node that is the actual leader of the configuration returns an index that covers its commit index, so the local singleton answer is only unsafe on the node that is no longer the voter.

No repair from the periodic path: after three heartbeat intervals and no replies from the current configuration, the removed leader is still leading at its old term and still answers with the same stale index.

The same enabling change of state - raftLog.committed advancing to an entry of the leader's term - is also produced inside switchToConfig, which calls r.maybeCommit() and, on success, only calls bcastAppend (raft.go:2013-2028). Applying a committed configuration change is a legal producer of that path: applyConfChange -> switchToConfig is invoked by the application whenever a configuration change is observed in Ready.CommittedEntries. When the applied change makes ProgressTracker.Committed() exceed raftLog.committed (removing a voter that is unreachable, or leaving a joint configuration whose outgoing half contains such a voter) and the entry at the resulting index carries the leader's term, the commit is performed with the postponed request still unreleased. Because the request was stored in pendingReadIndexMessages and not in readOnly.unconfirmedReads, no later heartbeat can carry its context, so the duty is not discharged by the periodic heartbeat round: the received request yields no ReadState for a local read and no MsgReadIndexResp for a forwarded one until an unrelated entry is committed (which again goes through the MsgAppResp path) or the client retries. The defect is therefore a lost duty on one of two enabling paths, scoped to a bounded interval: from the postponed request until the next commit outside switchToConfig. The returned index remains safe whenever the request is eventually released, because the recorded index is taken from raftLog.committed at release time and raftLog.committed never decreases; the defect is a bounded-liveness (unanswered request) issue, not a stale-read safety violation. limitations: Every scenario needs an application that applies the committed change removing the leading node while Config.StepDownOnRemoval is false and keeps that node running; applications that set the option, or that stop the removed node, do not reach the state.

The witnesses are at the ReadIndex contract level: the receipts show the index handed to the reader (locally or across the wire), or the request disappearing, or a round that counted a non-member - no state machine was run, so a served value that misses an entry is a consequence of the contract rather than a measured value.

The tick ratio is one heartbeat tick against ten election ticks in all five configurations; the multi-voter CheckQuorum receipt delivers no ticks to the voters, so the length of that exposure is unbounded within the receipt.
The lease-based configuration is still supported by source reading rather than by a retained receipt, and read-only rounds that fail (a leader that cannot reach a quorum) are not measured.
